axes.model_access:
It calls no model itself; it is an interface implementation called by clients.

Its design is tied to Claude's persistent-memory scenario (the README states plainly **"lets Claude remember information about the user across chats"**).
axes.runtime:
A local Node.js process communicating over stdio.

Data persists in a local JSONL file, with a lifecycle independent of the client process.
axes.local_files:
**Accesses only its own memory file** (by default under the memory directory); it provides no arbitrary file read/write tools.

The storage location can be set via a parameter; the actual accessible range depends on the permissions of that path.
axes.background:
The server process lives and dies with the client,

but **memory data persists on disk and survives restarts**.

A 2026-09-03 fix serialized graph mutations to avoid concurrent-write races.
axes.tools:
It provides 9 tools:

- create_entities, create_relations, add_observations, delete_entities, delete_observations, delete_relations, read_graph, search_nodes, open_nodes.

It also exposes one resource: `memory://knowledge-graph`.

**Including 3 delete tools** (delete_entities / delete_observations / delete_relations);
output is structured JSON, ready for direct consumption.
axes.context:
**This is the server's core capability**: cross-session persistent memory.

It stores entities, relations and observations in a knowledge-graph structure,
supporting retrieval (search_nodes) and read-by-name (open_nodes).
axes.permissions:
**No separate approval mechanism.**

The memory graph is global shared state; **every write affects all subsequent sessions**.

It provides 3 delete tools that can remove entities, observations and relations.

On 2026-09-03 a search_nodes query-length limit and a deduplication fix were added.
axes.fit:
Lets an Agent remember long-term information such as user preferences and project context across sessions.

Not a fit for scenarios needing audit or traceability (the graph is mutated in place).

mcp.transport:
stdio only. A local Node.js process communicating over standard input/output (launched via npx).

The official README (full-text verification 2026-10-08) has no official launch method for a remote transport.
mcp.auth:
No separate authentication layer. In stdio form it inherits the client user's permissions.

The memory file itself is unencrypted — **any process that can read that file can obtain all memory content**.
mcp.scope:
**The narrowest-scope class**: it reads and writes only its own memory file and provides no arbitrary file-access tools.

The permission risk lies not in file scope but in **content sensitivity** —

the memory may hold user preferences, project information and other privacy,
and the file is unencrypted with no independent access control.

sectionTitles.权限风险的特点: What is distinctive about its permission risk

sections.变更记录说明:
**This object has no standalone changelog page**; change records are in the directory's commit history:

| Date | Content |
|---|---|
| 2026-09-03 | Serialize graph mutations to avoid concurrent-write races |
| 2026-09-03 | Skip duplicate entities and relations within one batch |
| 2026-09-03 | Limit `search_nodes` query length |

**All three fixes landed on the same day (09-03)**, showing that release concentrated on stability. Especially the "concurrent-write race" — it means simultaneous multi-session reads/writes of memory once risked data corruption.

**If you use it in a multi-session environment, these three are worth reading at the source.**
sections.数据结构:
| Concept | Description | Example |
|---|---|---|
| **Entity** | a graph node with a unique name, type and observation list | `{name: "X", entityType: "person", observations: [...]}` |
| **Relation** | a directed connection between entities | `{from: "A", to: "B", relationType: "works_at"}` |
| **Observation** | an atomic fact attached to an entity | one fact per observation is recommended |

**Relations are stored in active voice**, e.g. `works_at` rather than "works at". This is an explicit convention in the docs.
sections.工具清单与读写属性:
| Tool | Attribute | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `read_graph` | read | read the whole graph |
| `search_nodes` | read | search nodes by condition |
| `open_nodes` | read | read specific nodes by name |
| `create_entities` | **write** | create entities |
| `create_relations` | **write** | create relations |
| `add_observations` | **write** | append observations to entities |
| `delete_entities` | **delete** | delete entities and their connections |
| `delete_observations` | **delete** | delete observations |
| `delete_relations` | **delete** | delete relations |

**6 read, 3 write, 3 delete**. Delete capability gets three tools — the thickest group in this entry.
sections.权限风险的特点:
Unlike other MCP servers, memory's risk is **not in file scope but in content**:

| Dimension | Assessment |
|---|---|
| File-access scope | **narrowest** — touches only its own memory file |
| Write impact | **global** — affects all subsequent sessions |
| Content sensitivity | **high** — may hold user preferences, project information |
| Access control | **none** — the file is unencrypted, no independent auth |

**Any process that can read that JSONL file obtains the entire memory.**

If you store sensitive information with it, this point must be considered.
sections.与 filesystem 的对比:
| Dimension | filesystem | memory |
|---|---|---|
| Access scope | directory allowlist (can be wide) | **only its own memory file (very narrow)** |
| Delete capability | not provided | **provides 3 delete tools** |
| Persistence | stateless | **graph persisted to disk** |
| Cross-session | not supported | **the core capability** |

**The trade-off is clear**: memory trades "limited capability but sensitive content" for "cross-session capability".
